name: Learn macramé knots
blurb: Four knots — square, half hitch, spiral and lark’s head — make plant hangers, wall hangings and bags. Rope is cheap and mistakes untie.
gear: A dowel or ring to mount on
A rack or hook to work from
Scissors and a comb for fringing
steps: Learn the lark’s head knot for mounting cords onto a dowel or ring.
Learn the square knot and its half-knot variant, which spirals when repeated.
Learn the double half hitch, both horizontal and diagonal, which is how you make lines and shapes.
Learn the gathering knot to bundle cords, essential for plant hangers.
Make a plant hanger as a first project, then a small wall hanging with a pattern.
Learn to measure cord: roughly four to six times the finished length per cord, doubled when mounted.
tips: Running out of cord halfway is the classic beginner disaster. Overestimate generously.
Consistent tension is what makes the pattern read. Work with the piece hanging under slight tension.
proof: A finished plant hanger or wall hanging using at least three knot types, with even tension.
